newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. ambassador praises Mexico's drug fight.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador praises Mexico's drug fight.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to Mexico praised the country's antinarcotics efforts on Monday and strongly suggested that Mexico would win the U.S. government's "certification" in fighting drug-trafficking.
"I think there has been improvement in the fight against Mexican drug-traffickers," Ambassador James Jones told reporters after meeting leaders of the conservative opposition National Action Party.
"My government wants to collaborate with Mexico, the enemy are the drug-traffickers. It will take a lot of cooperation between our countries to succeed in that fight."

President Bill Clinton must grade Mexico and 31 other countries at the end of the month in the "certification" process, Washington's annual review of other government's antinarcotics efforts. Countries that fail that test may be subjected to U.S. economic and trade sanctions.

Asked whether Mexico would receive such approval, given the recent arrest of its antinarcotics czar for drug links and allegations in the New York Times that two state governors are tainted by drugs corruption, Jones replied:
"Certification is a decision that requires two things -- the first is that there be cooperation between our countries and the second is that there be progress in the fight against drug-traffickers."
"As you know I think the answer is affirmative in both cases."
